title: Usage Gateway Compatibility Broker and Progressive Contracting
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: The console analytics pipeline sees frequent benign schema drift from SDK versions and partner integrations. Small field renames, optional field additions, and differing enum encodings are causing consumer-side errors and noisy alerts. Current strict validation rejects a non-trivial fraction of events or requires manual mapping and backfills, slowing feature rollout and inflating costs.

Goal: Implement a Compatibility Broker in the Usage Gateway that performs lightweight, policy-driven contract negotiation between producers and downstream consumers. The Broker should: 1) perform deterministic event fingerprinting and matching; 2) apply reversible transformation recipes for common drift patterns (rename, type coercion, enum mapping); 3) surface soft rejections and progressive enforcement windows; 4) emit structured telemetry for regression detection and automated backfills. This should reduce hard rejects by ~70% for common SDK drift while preserving safety for PII-sensitive fields.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Gateway routes events through Compatibility Broker by default for console usage events. 2) Broker supports at least three transform types: rename, integer<->string coercion, and enum alias mapping via rule templates. 3) Admin UI can mark a rule as dry-run (soft enforcement) and schedule automatic enforcement after an observation window. 4) Observable metrics: transform_count, soft_reject_count, hard_reject_count, rule_hit_rate, and top-5 producer fingerprints. 5) No increase in median ingest latency > 12ms at p95 under 10k rps load. 6) Integration tests and a migration runbook are documented in Confluence.
design_decisions:
- Use a rule-first model stored in Redis with versioned rule IDs so we can roll forward/rollback quickly.
- Perform transformations in the gateway node process to avoid extra network hops; heavy validation moved to an async validator service for deep checks.
- Progressive enforcement: default to dry-run for 7 days, then auto-escalate if error ratio below threshold.
- Rule templates authored by a new DSL inspired by previous mapping patterns rather than ad-hoc JSON blobs.
- Sensitive fields (marked by tag) bypass transformations and always go through strict validation.
implementation_notes:
- New route /v1/gateway/compatibility-evaluate for dry-run diagnostics.
- Add a lightweight fingerprint: (event_type, schema_hash_v2, producer_id, top_field_signatures) to group similar events.
- Transformation engine uses an ordered pipeline: detect -> apply-coercions -> rename -> enum-map -> emit.
- Store example payloads for each fingerprint for rule authoring UI.
- Backfill system will generate mapping PRs for BigQuery ingestion tier when a rule is promoted to enforced.
- Fallback behavior: when a transformation fails, return original payload with metadata header broker_status=partial_transform.
progress_updates: 2026-02-09: Kickoff with Console backend, Analytics, and DX SDK teams. Collected top 200 failure signatures from last 30d.
2026-02-16: Prototype rule DSL and in-process transformer implemented. Benchmarked median add latency ~6ms at p95 with 1k rps on dev nodes.
2026-02-25: Security review requested; identified three sensitive field markers that must be excluded from any auto-transforms.
2026-03-02: Integration test harness wired against staging pipeline; added synthetic drift scenarios for rename and enum aliasing.
2026-03-07: UX stub for rule management in Console created (PR link below). Decided to keep default dry-run window at 7 days and escalation threshold at 0.5% error rate.
2026-03-10: Load test at 8k rps shows p95 ingest latency increase of 11ms; memory overhead per gateway process +18MB. Preparing capacity plan for Dedicated lanes.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Over-eager transforms could hide producer bugs. Mitigation: default to dry-run, rule audit trail, and explicit owner assignment for every rule.
- Risk: Performance regression at high throughput. Mitigation: keep path lightweight; offload heavy checks to async validator and add per-producer sampling.
- Risk: Regulatory/PII exposure. Mitigation: sensitive-field tagging enforced in security review; transformations not allowed on tagged fields.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for DSL parsing, transform application, and fingerprinting.
- Integration tests: run synthetic drift scenarios and assert transformed payloads match expected examples.
- Load tests: p50/p95/p99 with and without transformations at 10k rps baseline.
- Chaos test: simulate Redis rule store failover and ensure gateway falls back to pass-through mode with alerting.
rollout_plan:
1) Canary 1% of producers -> validate soft rejection metrics and rule hit rates. 2) Canary 10% with auto-scaling enabled. 3) Broaden to 50% and start promoting stable rules to enforced. 4) Full rollout once p95 latency within SLO and error rates negligible.
Backout: revoke enforced rules and toggle gateway to pass-through if hard_reject_count spikes > 3x baseline.
review_feedback: PM (Lena Ortiz): prioritize rule audit metadata and owner fields so we can trace why a transform was applied.
Security (Omar Levy): block transformations for fields with pii_tag=true; add KMS annotation for stored example payloads.
Design (Priya Nair): keep rule UI workflow minimal — author -> dry-run -> approve -> enforce. Provide diff view for transformed payloads.
